ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The area of the coil abcd is $0.05\mathrm{m}^{2}$, with a total of 100 turns. The total resistance of the coil is $\mathbf{r}=1\Omega$, and the external resistance is $\mathbf{R}=9\Omega$. The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $\mathrm{B}=\frac{1}{\pi}\mathrm{T}$. When the coil rotates at a constant speed of $300\mathrm{r/min}$.

1. If timing starts when the coil is at the neutral plane, write the expression for the instantaneous value of the induced electromotive force in the coil.
2. What is the instantaneous value of the electromotive force when the coil rotates through $\frac{1}{60}s$?
3. In the circuit, what is the reading of the ammeter? (Please keep the answer to 3 significant figures)
4. In the circuit, what is the reading on the voltmeter? (Please keep the answer to 3 significant figures)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the figure is the coil abcd, located in a uniform magnetic field indicated by “×”; the coil is connected through the lower conducting wire into a closed external circuit. In the lower circuit, there is an external resistor R and an ammeter A connected in series in the main loop, and a voltmeter V is connected in parallel across the two ends of the external circuit, used to measure the terminal voltage across the two ends of the external resistor. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives N=100, S=0.05 m^2, B=1/π T, coil internal resistance r=1 Ω, external resistor R=9 Ω, rotational speed n=300 r/min=5 r/s, so the angular velocity ω=2πn=10π rad/s. The maximum value of the induced electromotive force E_m=NBSω=100×0.05×(1/π)×10π=50 V. Since timing starts from the neutral plane, the induced electromotive force starts from 0 and changes according to a sine law, so e=50 sin(10πt) V. When t=1/60 s, e=50 sin(10π/60)=50 sin(π/6)=25 V. Meter readings use effective values; the effective value of the electromotive force E=E_m/√2=50/√2 V, and the total resistance R+r=10 Ω, therefore the ammeter reading I=E/(R+r)=50/(√2×10)=3.535... A≈3.54 A. The voltmeter measures the voltage across the two ends of the external resistor R, U=IR=3.535...×9=31.819... V≈31.8 V.
